extracted.intended_audience: The people of the State of New York; engaged citizens and voters considering ratification of the proposed U.S. Constitution
extracted.subtask_description: A persuasive political essay (Federalist Paper) addressed to citizens to assess and defend the proposed federal Constitution, explaining difficulties of framing government and rebutting objections. Aimed at guiding public judgment about adoption and ratification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Moderation and candor in evaluating public measures
rubrics_metrics.description: Public measures are rarely investigated with that spirit of moderation which is essential to a just estimate of their real tendency to advance or obstruct the public good.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Readers should approach the Constitution with a temper favorable to a just estimate (not predetermined to condemn or praise). The papers solicit those who combine sincere zeal for the country's happiness with a disposition to fair judgment, avoiding partisan biases and extreme dispositions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allowances for human fallibility in judging the convention's work
rubrics_metrics.description: A faultless plan was not to be expected; keep in mind that the convention, as a body of men, were liable to fallibility and that critics themselves are also but men and should not assume infallibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make allowances for errors chargeable to human fallibility, and avoid rejudging with presumptions of perfection; consider the limitations under which the convention operated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consider novelty and lack of precedents when assessing a new constitution
rubrics_metrics.description: The novelty of the undertaking: other confederacies cannot supply a full precedent, they can only serve as beacons indicating what to avoid, not what to pursue.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expect unavoidable uncertainty and the need to avoid past errors rather than to copy any prior model; evaluate the plan in light of unprecedented circumstances and the impossibility of perfect precedent-based solutions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Balance stability and energy of government with republican liberty
rubrics_metrics.description: Combining the requisite stability and energy in government with the inviolable attention due to liberty and to the republican form is difficult and essential.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether the proposed plan attains sufficient energy for security and execution of laws, and sufficient stability for national character and repose, without sacrificing republican principles like derivation of power from the people and short durations of office.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accept indeterminacy in delineating federal and state authorities
rubrics_metrics.description: Marking the proper line of partition between the authority of the general and that of the State governments is a difficult task, subject to delicate shades and minute gradations like those in metaphysical or natural distinctions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize that precise boundaries may elude human sagacity; expect litigation, adjudication, and practical development to clarify obscure points over time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Account for ambiguity arising from language and expression
rubrics_metrics.description: Perspicuity requires that ideas be distinctly formed and expressed by words appropriate to them; no language is so copious as to supply words for every complex idea, so definitions may be rendered inaccurate by the inaccuracy of terms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When evaluating provisions, allow for unavoidable linguistic ambiguity, especially for complex and novel objects; understand that some uncertainty is intrinsic and will be liquidated by future cases and decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Anticipate compromise between large and small states and local interests
rubrics_metrics.description: Interfering pretensions of the larger and smaller States, and a variety of local interests and jealousies, would likely compel sacrifices of theoretical propriety to extraneous considerations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expect and accept compromises necessary to secure union; assess provisions in light of the political realities and necessity of accommodating competing state interests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prefer practical effectiveness over theoretical symmetry
rubrics_metrics.description: Under the pressure of many difficulties, the convention may have been forced into deviations from artificial structure and regular symmetry which an abstract theorist might prefer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Value arrangements that surmount practical difficulties and secure unanimity, even if they lack perfect theoretical regularity; practical survivability can justify asymmetries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Value exemption from factional animosities and sacrifice of private interests
rubrics_metrics.description: The convention must, in a singular degree, have enjoyed an exemption from the pestilential influence of party animosities; deputations were accommodated by the final act or induced to accede by conviction of the public good.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Give weight to evidence that framers acted beyond factional interest and prioritized public good; favor schemes that show capacity to transcend partisan aims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accept that a better (not perfect) system should replace a worse one
rubrics_metrics.description: It is not necessary that the new system be perfect; it is sufficient that the existing Confederation is more imperfect.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When choosing between systems, judges should prefer a materially improved system over retention of a demonstrably defective one, even if the new plan has imperfections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Require objectors to propose coherent alternatives
rubrics_metrics.description: If critics advise against the proposed remedy, they should at least agree among themselves on some other remedy to be substituted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Weight is diminished for objections that only reject without offering a united, viable substitute; prudent action favors unanimously recommended remedies by qualified advisers rather than fractured objections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compare objections to the proposed plan against defects of the current Confederation
rubrics_metrics.description: Many capital objections urged against the new system lie with tenfold weight against the existing Confederation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate objections by asking whether the same or worse problems afflict the current system; use comparative judgment to assess whether change is warranted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ensure that conferred powers are effective, not nugatory
rubrics_metrics.description: The Confederation declares certain powers to be absolutely necessary while rendering them absolutely nugatory; effective powers must be granted or assumed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Scrutinize whether powers given to a federal government are backed by means of execution; nominal powers without effect invite disorder and dangerous compensatory powers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Anticipate long-term practical consequences (e.g., national stock from western territory)
rubrics_metrics.description: Future management of western territory will likely become a national stock and a source of revenue, and Congress has assumed administration of this stock.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider how present decisions will shape future resources and power; evaluate institutional arrangements with an eye to foreseeable economic and political developments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recognize that objections often spring from diverse, inconsistent fears
rubrics_metrics.description: Objectors disagree widely—some fear monarchy, others aristocracy, some fear legislative-executive intermixture, others the want of a bill of rights—rarely are two objectors agreed on particulars.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat diffuse and internally inconsistent criticism as less persuasive; demand specific, internally coherent objections rather than generalized alarmism.
